Budget Workshop
AGENDA
A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
June 6, 2012
02:00 A.M.
City Hall Council Chambers
24300 Narbonne Avenue
1.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.
Roll Call
2.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. When addressing the Council, please come to the podium and give your name and address for the record. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
SCHEDULED MATTERS
3.
BUDGET WORKSHOP - PROPOSED FY 2012/13 BUDGET
Discussion and possible direction to staff regarding proposed budget for FY 2012/2013. Presented by Interim City Manager Sugano and Administrative Services Director Chavez.
2012-06-06 Staff report #3
ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 24300 Narbonne Avenue.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at 310 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.

MINUTES OF AN ADJOURNED MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  June 6, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

An adjourned meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 6 p.m. on
Wednesday, June 6, 2012, in the Commission Room, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne
Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Estrada, Sanchez, Savidan, Traina, and Mayor Gazeley. Also
present were Interim City Manager Sugano, Public Works Director Damasse, City
Attorney Hogin, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Parks and Recreation Director
Blount, Community Services Director Greg McPherron and Assistant City Clerk
Shumway.

2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

None.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

3. BUDGET WORKSHOP - PROPOSED FY 2012/13 BUDGET

Interim City Manager Sugano provided an overview of the FY 2012-13 budget. Sugano
stated that general fund revenues remain relatively flat and general fund expenses are
projected to exceed revenues. Sugano noted that the general fund will be balanced
through the use of $261,964 from the undesignated general fund balance. According to
Sugano, the goal is to eliminate the shortfall in the budget through budget reductions in
the general fund and reducing general fund subsidies to special revenue funds.
Specifically, Sugano noted that the landscape maintenance district subsidy, in the
amount of $8,205, has been reduced to $5,000, due to a reduction in landscape
maintenance agreement costs. Sugano also pointed out that the park athletic fund and
gas tax subsidies have been eliminated through budget reductions. Furthermore,
Sugano stated that some positions have been frozen or eliminated, and for FY 2012-13,
staff is recommending a total of 46 full-time positions.

  June 6, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 1 of 5
 Administrative Services Director Chavez informed City Council that staff tried to reduce
general fund expenditures, as the use of carryover from the general fund is not
sustainable in the long term. Chavez continued by providing an overview of estimated
revenues, including: property tax revenue, which is projected at $1.6 million, a $55,000
increase from the previous fiscal year; sales tax, which is projected at $1.28 million, a
$73,000 increase from last year; and motor vehicle in-lieu tax, which is projected at
$1.66 million, a decrease of $99,000 from last year.

Interim City Manager Sugano stated that staff included $20,000 in the FY 2012-13
budget to retain the services of a specialized consultant to study the salary allocations
to the water fund. In response to Councilmember Sanchez’s question regarding the
years to be reviewed in terms of salary allocations, Sugano answered that the scope of
the study would include a review of the duties for each position receiving allocations in
order to see if the allocations are justified, and in turn reflect the actual time spent by the
employee on matters related to the Water Enterprise. Sugano further noted that the
scope of the study could include additional years, if staff is directed to do so by City
Council. Councilmember Traina commented that in 1995, salary allocations were
significantly changed, and for the review Councilmember Traina suggested asking each
employee, whose positions are partly allocated to the Water Enterprise Fund, whether
the position allocation percentage reflects their actual time spent on water issues.
Councilmember Traina further noted that the proposed $20,000 consultant cost was too
high and suggested that staff conduct the salary allocation review. Sugano responded
that the salary allocation review would involve some fiscal analysis, and therefore expert
review would be recommended and more appropriate.

Interim City Manager Sugano stated that staff is recommending the following allocations
for the general fund overage:

  •  $261,964 to balance the general fund budget;
  •  $100,000 for Islamic Center of South Bay litigation;
  •  $50,000 for the Street Improvement Fund; and
  •  The remaining $60,364 as reserves to fund unexpected expenses.

Mayor Gazeley commented that when he took office as Mayor, the budget shortfall was
$1.4 million, which was then reduced to $425,000; this year the deficit was reduced by
50% more.

City Council started reviewing the budget page by page.

Councilmember Traina suggested looking at increasing some other revenues, such as
transient lodging tax or business licenses. City Attorney Hogin informed Council that
transient lodging tax increases must go through a ballot measure and be in conjunction
with municipal elections.

  June 6, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 2 of 5
 Councilmember Savidan asked whether the amount of $5,000 for bike patrol was
justifiable. Community Services Director McPherron responded that the $5,000 pays for
personnel costs only, and he requested to keep that amount budgeted.

Councilmember Estrada suggested that City Council consider some reductions in
different parts of the budget to fund the Core Deputy position, which could have a
budget shortfall if the COPs funding is not continued. Councilmember Estrada asked if
Council would consider moving the bike patrol budgeted amount of $5,000 towards the
Core Deputy position. Discussion followed regarding the benefits of having a bike patrol
as a crime prevention unit, and it was agreed that the bike patrol would be funded at the
requested amount of $5,000.

Community Services Director McPherron pointed out that CDBG funds were
substantially reduced, and stated that staff had budgeted some money toward the
purchase of CDBG funds from other jurisdictions.

Responding to Councilmember Traina's question about increasing the landscape
maintenance assessment, Interim City Manager Sugano stated that such an increase
would require a ballot measure, in accordance with Proposition 218.

Councilmember Traina encouraged staff to apply for grants through the Water
Replenishment District. Mayor Gazeley noted that larger cities have more preference in
receiving those types of grants; however, the City could work with other small
jurisdictions on lobbying for such funding. Interim City Manager Sugano stated that staff
is looking at those and other grant opportunities.

Discussion followed on whether the entry fee for the Railroad Museum was appropriate,
and it was decided that an increase in the entry fee would not be recommended at this
time.

Councilmember Estrada recommended reducing the travel expenses for City Council
from $3,500 to $2,000 a year, per Councilmember. Discussion followed on whether the
reduction would be sufficient enough to cover all the travel expenses for City Council.
Councilmember Estrada made a motion to cut the travel expenses for City
Councilmembers to $2,000 per Councilmember and $3,000 for the Mayor, and that
funds not spent by Councilmembers could be used to cover additional expenses for the
Mayor. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion. The motion carried as follows:

Ayes: Estrada, Savidan, and Traina
Nays: Sanchez and Mayor Gazeley

In response to Councilmember Traina's questions on whether the salary allocations to
the Water Enterprise Fund were accurate, and how the allocation percentages were
established, Interim City Manager Sugano replied that no comprehensive study was
ever done and that the allocation percentages were based on historic numbers.
Councilmember Traina stated that he did not believe that the City needs to pay $20,000

  June 6, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 3 of 5
 for a consultant to review salary allocations. Sugano responded that until a request for
proposal goes out, the true cost will not be known. The City Council concluded that
detailed discussions regarding salary allocations to the Water Enterprise Fund will be
more appropriate after a consultant reviews the salary allocations.

In response to Councilmember Savidan’s question regarding the reduction in cost of
auditing services, Administrative Services Director Chavez explained that the decrease
is due to the lower bid amount of the newly selected auditing firm, which is $28,000 per
year.

Councilmember Estrada suggested reducing the special expenses line item under the
Community Services Department.  Community Services Department Director
McPherron stated that special expenses cover business license background checks for
applicants. Councilmember Estrada moved to reduce the special expenses line item
under the Community Services Department to $3,000. Mayor Gazeley seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

Councilmember Estrada requested allocating the $30,000 that is currently budgeted for
DUI and seat belt enforcement towards the Core Deputy position. The City Council
agreed with Councilmember Estrada's request.

Discussion followed on whether $24,373 for Sheriff’s services could be budgeted under
the Water Enterprise Fund.  City Attorney Hogin responded that the Sheriff’s
Department provides security checks at the reservoir, and those services are directly
related to the Water Enterprise Fund. For future budgeting purposes, and to reflect the
actual cost for reservoir security monitoring by Sheriff’s Department, Councilmember
Savidan suggested asking the Sheriff’s Department to keep a log of when the area is
patrolled and provide those logs to the City.

Councilmember Estrada recommended removing the contingency line item under the
Parks and Recreation Department since the funds were not utilized in FY 2011-12; with
the consensus of the Council it was agreed that the line item be reduced from $10,000
to $2,500.

Responding to Councilmember Traina's question on whether the City subsidizes the
Golf Tournament, Interim City Manager Sugano stated that money raised covers the
expenses and an additional $10,000 goes towards funding youth programs.

Discussion followed regarding the street sweeping contract. Prior to FY 2012-13, the
street sweeping program was budgeted under a different department. According to
Public Works Director Damasse the cost of street sweeping increased due to the higher
bids received, which included contingency and CPI increases. Councilmember Traina
asked staff to address the issue of street sweepers going too fast.

Councilmember Traina noted that the professional services line item under the Public
Works Department seemed high. Public Works Director Damasse stated that the repair

  June 6, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 4 of 5
 costs for the Scada Integrator were included in this line item, due to the fact that the
warranty for the Scada Integrator has expired.

Councilmember Traina inquired as to why the electricity costs for the Public Works
Department had increased, and Public Works Director Damasse responded that water
blending and future work were being anticipated for FY 2012-13, as last year the
reservoir was not operational. Councilmember Sanchez suggested reducing the
electricity line item to $10,000. Director Damasse replied that if water blending and
work at the reservoir would be suspended, then the savings in this line item would go
toward the purchase of water from Metropolitan to cover the difference.

Councilmember Traina asked for more detail regarding the Capital Improvement
Projects budget. Interim City Manager Sugano responded that staff will make a more
detailed presentation, with input from the new City Manager, regarding the CIP budget
sometime in July or August 2012.

Councilmember Traina asked that the budgets be made available via the City's website.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:39 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Lena Shumway, CMC
Assistant City Clerk

  June 6, 2012 Council Minutes  Page 5 of 5
